decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front, not the side, and a short length of chain hangs from it down his chest. This is not above anyone's head, so it does not break the rule against vertical chains. A hanging lantern lights the hold warmly, so it is dim rather than near darkness. The pale slits overhead read as gaps in the deck seams, not open sky, which fits 1.3. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists under the manacles, wrist chain, ankle cuffs with hobble chain, barefoot. His right hand lies flat on the planks. A ragged ochre flap covers his left forearm, so no brand shows. The image is tilted hard and upright boards split the pens. Pen chains run collar to collar and rise to the beams at a slant. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Hands and feet are sound. The dark, plain ceiling at top right easily holds both captions, and the dark foreground planks at bottom left are a second option. v01 to v04 were not offered as candidates in this round (they show open sky and storm through the hull).

Acceptable, with minor points only. The computed task lists the cast as [nagoji] and only the CAPTION line. Script 1.2 and the ch03-r8 INDEX both have Keshavrao in the panel and give him the line "Storm." The frame correctly shows him on the right with the script's look: young, faint moustache, hacked short hair, grey-brown tunic, no stud, eyes up to the deck. If the letterer uses the script copy, his mouth is at about x 0.577, y 0.332, and the short balloon fits in the dark ceiling above and between the two heads (about x 0.47 to 0.60, y 0 to 0.12). Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, small round gold stud in the lobe, torn ochre sleeveless tunic that matches panel 1.1, bandaged wrists, hinged collar with a front ring, and eyes half closed. His anatomical left forearm, the one at the centre next to Keshavrao, is bandaged most of the way to the elbow, and its inner face is turned toward his body, so the brand stays hidden. It is not the ragged tunic flap that 1.1 asks for, but it meets the bible's rule that the arm is covered or turned from camera. The setting is the dim, lantern-lit wooden hold, with no sky and no guards, so it matches 1.1. There are no painted balloons, text, noose, blood or anachronism, and all four hands are sound. Minor points: the pen chain runs almost straight across at chest height through both collar rings instead of drooping in loops, though it is never vertical. The skin on Nagoji's shoulder shows a faint crosshatch texture from upscaling. The iron band on the left pillar has ornamental scrollwork, but none of it reads as letters. For the caption "Ships speak when they are in trouble.", the plain dark plank wall and ceiling at the right (about x 0.73 to 0.99, y 0.02 to 0.40) is the best spot, clear of both faces and all hands. A strip across the dhoti knees at the bottom (y 0.88 to 1.0) is a second option.
decisions.tails_note: Keshavrao's mouth point taken from the reviewer's issues text; the orchestrator's selection args omitted his line

decisions.issues: Minor only. The boot shadows are cast straight onto the underside of the solid deck planks, which is physically loose but clearly reads as the scripted beat of running feet crossing overhead. The frame has no text, no noose (the ropes are coils and lashings), no open sky and no painted balloons. Grey-white light cuts through the seams and water drips down onto the beam. The low-detail dark planking along the top band (roughly y 0 to 0.2, left and right) takes both jagged balloons without covering the shadows. Tails go to the top edge because the sailors are off panel above.

Minor. The guard's raised hand grips the edge of the canvas awning, not the hatch frame. Besides the cross-belt he wears a narrow waist belt (not wide, and no key ring). Faint plank highlights at the far left (about x 0.01 to 0.07, y 0.49 to 0.54) could suggest stencil marks at a squint, but a contrast check shows wood grain, not letterforms. The guard look matches: lean, dark-bearded, steel morion, soaked buff jerkin with cross-belt over a shirt, flintlock in hand, rain pouring through the hatch as the awning is dragged across. v01 is preferred: its small top-left box sits on dark beams clear of the musket hand, while v02's tall left box reaches down to the hand gripping the musket.
decisions.erase_note: v03 is an erase-only edit of v01 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited
v02 is an erase-only edit of v01 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: v12 is clean and matches the beat. The musket lies large in the foreground against the beam at the foot of the ladder, grey light comes down the hatch, and the chained pen rows face it with collar chains slack. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged wrists, and his left forearm is covered by bandage and manacle. Keshavrao also matches: short hacked hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, no stud. Minor points: Nagoji and Keshavrao look ahead rather than plainly down at the musket, and the background prisoners are nearly all bearded men who look alike. Both captions have room on the dark ceiling beams across the top (x 0.05-0.7, y 0-0.13), and the wet floor at lower right is also clear. Backup v10 is weaker. The musket is small in the lower-right corner rather than dominating the foreground, there is no ladder, and a highlight on Keshavrao's earlobe comes close to reading as a stud.

Clean. The guard is seen from behind in a morion and buff jerkin with cross-belt, silhouetted in the open hatch against rain and storm light, head turned toward the deck, never looking down. The painted balloons have long tails, but both point at the guard (the correct speaker), and the drawn balloons will cover them. The frame is 2.65:1 and the slot is about 3.97:1, so set visible_rect to roughly [0,0,2043,515] to keep the hatch, guard and beams without letterboxing. v05 is the same art pre-letterboxed to a 5.35:1 strip, which the contain fit would place thinner than the slot. v02 is an outdoor fort scene (reject). v03 and v04 are acceptable but have oversized painted balloons.
decisions.erase_note: v06 is an erase-only edit of v01 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: v09 is a proper close two-shot with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right. Nagoji looks up at the hatch, where water drips through at top left. Keshavrao looks off-panel right, toward where the musket lay in 2.1. Seawater threads across the boards around their bare feet and hobble chains. Collars, collar chain and wrist manacles are all correct. Nagoji has his moustache, only light captivity stubble on the chin, the gold stud, and fully bandaged forearms, so the brand stays hidden. Keshavrao matches his lock. Hands are sound. Minor points: they sit on the floor against the hull, not on the raised pen shelf seen in 2.1, and lettering space is tight. Usable space is the dark hull wall between and above the heads (x 0.42-0.58, y 0-0.25), the top-right strip over Keshavrao (x 0.72-0.85, y 0-0.08) and the dark right-hand wall (x 0.85-1.0, y 0-0.4). Backup v07 has correct characters and gazes, but it is a wide shot with the pair far apart rather than a close shot, and the water on the floor reads as a wet sheen rather than a thread of water.

Minor. The floor carries a shallow sheet of water, and water cascades down the ladder steps, rather than a single thin thread (it matches the 2.3 stairwell). The current does curl around the stock. The flintlock (cock and frizzen visible) lies against the beam, and the ladder rises into grey storm light. The visible strip (y 187-575) is exactly the 5.09:1 slot, with a clear caption band over the dark beams at upper left. v04 is the same art full-frame; it needs a crop to about [0,245,1959,630] and would lose most of the sky. v01 is also acceptable, but its current runs by the barrel rather than the stock, and it needs a heavy crop. v02 is an unrelated scene (reject).
decisions.erase_note: v06 is an erase-only edit of v05 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor issues. The wide, distant view shows the broadside surge: water rushes down the aisle into the pens and the collar-to-collar pen chains snap sideways along the rows, never upward. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism (glass lanterns are fine on a Portuguese ship). Minor points: the rendering is more photographic and cinematic than the inked neighbouring panels; the extras are bare-chested in loincloths rather than grey and brown rags; the tilt is modest and the 'almost weightless' moment is not really shown, since the men are bracing, which reads a little like galley rowers. The caption fits cleanly in the large dark ceiling area at top left (x 0.02 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Acceptable. This is a clean edit of the previously accepted v03 with the painted balloons removed and no artefacts left behind. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic with a ragged flap covering his left forearm, bandaged wrists, hinged collar. He shouts down the line while the men beside him copy the overhead grip. Deviations: he grips the beam with his hands apart instead of hooking both forearms over it with his wrists together, and his collar chain hangs down the front from the centre of the collar instead of drooping to one side from a side ring. The blue-lit grating at upper right reads as storm light through a hatch grating, not open sky. There is room for lettering over the low-detail beams at top left (x 0.0 to 0.3, y 0.0 to 0.18) and top right (x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.0 to 0.2), clear of the raised hands.

Minor only. A thin black frame border and white margin are painted inside the image (crop them at placement). Nagoji's wrist chain runs longer than a forearm and meets his collar chain near Keshavrao's cuff. There is a small pale window-like patch at the extreme top-left edge. Otherwise sound: the lantern-lit hold matches pages 2 and 3. Nagoji is on the left (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, ochre rags) and clamps his bandaged hand on Keshavrao's forearm, with the inner forearm turned from camera. Keshavrao is on the right (ragged short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags, collar with the side pen chain, bare hands), sliding away and reaching for a barrel. The chain meets his cuff. There is no text, and the panel is silent as the script calls for. Rejected: v02 and v03 show Keshavrao with no iron collar, and v03 also has a bright storm window. v04 puts Nagoji in a white tunic with a red sash. v01 is on the open deck with guards and sky.

Acceptable. This is a tight two-shot with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, faces close and water streaming down them. Nagoji is on-model: curled moustache, light captivity stubble only, gold stud, ochre rags, bandaged wrists, collar. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar, no ear stud. The collar-to-collar chain droops between them. Nagoji's left forearm shows at the bottom from the outer side with a bandaged wrist and no brand, which is acceptable. Lettering room is limited to the dark top band (x 0.0 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.16) and the dark left edge (x 0.0 to 0.18, y 0.16 to 0.45). The two long lines may need balloons that just touch the top of Nagoji's hair, but no face would be covered.

Acceptable. Keshavrao is alone and on-model: short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown torn tunic, hinged collar with a side ring, no ear stud. His eyes are wide in the gloom, and lightning glows through the seams overhead. Minor points: the lightning does not really light half his face, which is lit evenly and warmly; the render is darker and more photographic than 3.4; his eyes glance screen-right, although Nagoji is off-panel to the left (placed by 3.4 and by the collar chain leaving the frame at left). The large, plain, dark plank wall on the left (x 0.02 to 0.5, y 0.02 to 0.6) holds all three balloons easily. The tail for Nagoji's off-panel line points to the left edge.

Minor only. The over-the-shoulder framing works: Keshavrao is seen from behind (short hair, grey-brown tunic, collar) and Nagoji matches his sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, collar, bandaged fists, ankle cuffs with a hobble chain), with his fist round the drooping chain. His left arm is wrapped in a ragged ochre sleeve rather than the sleeveless tunic, which still keeps the brand hidden. The forearm-long chain between his wrists is not clearly shown. The plank bowing inward behind him is not distinct. Water sheets down the walls, which is heavier than the scripted spray but reads as seepage through the hull, not rain. There is no painted text or balloons. For lettering, use the low-detail wall at upper right (about x 0.68 to 0.98, y 0.03 to 0.40) and the upper centre (x 0.30 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17), away from Nagoji's face.

Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged wet hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, iron collar. The ghost of a smile is there, and there is no text. There is a painted white margin with a thin black frame line about 20 px in on every edge. Trim about 22 px from each side before placing it, or the panel gets a double border (tail and face fractions above refer to the untrimmed image). The background planks are warm, bright and softly blurred, with a slight mosaic upscale texture. That is lighter than the dark, cold-lit hold in 4.1, but acceptable for a tight close-up. For lettering, use the plain wall at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.97, y 0.04 to 0.45). Tail point override (2026-10-01, r4 review): aimed at the right side of the jaw at mouth level, so the tail runs down beside the head and stops at the cheek, not across the eye.

This is the closed hold, wide, with lightning lines through the deck seams and chained men clinging to beams and each other, mouths open and eye-whites showing. There is no text and no painted boxes. Minor points: the light comes through plank seams rather than specifically round a hatch cover, and it reads as a dim blue flicker more than one harsh white freeze-frame. The third man from the left has a faint reddish flush on his forehead. It is diffuse, with no gash or drip, so it does not read as gore at print size. The second man (curly hair, moustache) has stubble and no ear stud, so he should not be mistaken for Nagoji. Put the caption in the dark ceiling planks along the top (x 0.30 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.12).

v02 is acceptable. The camera looks straight up at the underside of the deck at the moment of impact. The planks bow downward, and sheets of water and grit pour through the seams while the beams and hull timbers stay whole. There are no figures, no text, no sky and no open hatch. The painted blank balloons sit upper left (before the impact) and lower right (after it), with no tails. That is right, because both speakers are sailors off panel above the deck. Both balloons bleed off the frame edges, but the letterer covers them. v01 is rejected: its painted balloon tails point at men in the hold instead of off-panel sailors, the ceiling shows bright openings, and it adds figures the script does not call for.
decisions.erase_note: v03 is an erase-only edit of v02 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Nagoji is on the left and matches his sheet: moustache, gold ear stud, clean chin with light captivity stubble, collar, bandaged wrists, manacles with a short chain, no brand visible. Keshavrao is on the right and matches his: short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar. They are waist-deep, with chains dragging in the surge and a bearded prisoner gasping behind them. The ring bolted in the beam at upper right is clear, with the chain running to it. Hands are sound and there is no text. Minor points: Keshavrao shouts with his chin up but is not tight at Nagoji's ear (the prisoner sits between them), and he looks up-left rather than toward the ring. The background prisoner wears a small gold ear stud, though his full beard keeps him distinct from Nagoji. The warm golden light is warmer than the cool blue of 4.1. For lettering, use the ceiling beams across the top (the PRISONER balloon about x 0.35 to 0.55, y 0.03 to 0.20; the KESHAVRAO balloon about x 0.56 to 0.82, y 0.02 to 0.20), keeping the ring at about x 0.90, y 0.10 clear.

v02 is acceptable. It shows the ring bolted under the overhead beam, cracks and lifting splinters around the plate, and the chain rising at a slant from out of frame lower left, inside a lantern-lit hold that matches 4.5 and 5.2. Minor points: the plate uses crisp hexagonal nuts that look slightly machine-made, the chain is heavier than the collar chain in neighbouring panels, and the hold looks dry here. The painted box upper left sits over plain beam and gets covered. v01 is rejected because it is set outdoors in daylight with palm trees and a stockade fence, so it is not the closed hold.
decisions.erase_note: v03 is an erase-only edit of v02 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: v06 is acceptable. The ring hangs from one bolt in a freshly splintered beam, and its chain drops slack into the water at the far end of the row. The row of collared, manacled prisoners is dragged sideways and leans to the left. Nagoji (front left) matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged hands, hinged collar. Keshavrao (second) matches his. Water pours through the deck seams, and the hull timbers stay whole, as 4.4 requires. The caption box upper left covers only ceiling. The backup v04 is weaker because the ring chain runs taut at a diagonal instead of sagging into the water. v05 is rejected because the hull is smashed open to the sea and rain at right, which breaks 4.4. v03 is rejected because the ring hangs detached from the chain, which anticipates 5.5. v02 is rejected because the lead prisoner is a bearded curly-haired man who reads as a bearded Nagoji, and nobody wears collars. v01 is rejected because it is set outside the ship on open sea with guards on deck.
decisions.erase_note: v07 is an erase-only edit of v06 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Clean pick. v06 is v05 (the version already accepted) with the painted balloon removed, and the repainted ceiling, beams and barrels in the upper right show no leftover marks. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, short-chained manacles, hinged collar with a side ring. The tunic flap covers his left forearm down to the bandage, so the brand stays hidden. He rounds on the prisoners with teeth bared while they cry out with raised fists and reaching hands. The waist-deep flooded hold, warm light, barrels and dripping seams match 5.2 and 5.4. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism, and all hands are sound. Two minor points: a small grated opening at the top left shows rain outside, which reads as a hull scuttle rather than open sky; and the left-hand pen chain disappears behind Nagoji's hip. Neither needs a regeneration. Put the single NAGOJI balloon over the low-detail beams and barrels up and to the right of his head, at about x 0.62 to 0.82 and y 0.03 to 0.30. It covers no face and no hand.

v12 is the pick. Nagoji is on the left and matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, loose curly hair, ochre rags, bandaged wrists. Keshavrao is on the right with short hair, a grey-brown tunic and no ear stud, but his moustache is a little heavier than the 'faint' one on his sheet. Both haul a taut pen chain level in their manacled fists with their heels braced on the pen plank. The chain rises to the ring, which hangs by its last bolt from a splintered beam at upper right. That matches the ring's position and damage in 5.1, 5.2 and 4.5, and the pull is on their fists and shoulders, with no upward pull on any neck. There is no painted text, no noose and no gore, and the hands are sound. The dark ceiling from the upper middle to the upper left (about x 0.33 to 0.80, y 0.02 to 0.25) gives clear room for both Nagoji balloons. Minor flaws: (1) The water only splashes around the plank at ankle height, shallower than the waist-deep flood in 4.5 and 5.3. The ship's roll can explain it, but it is a small continuity drift. (2) Each ankle cuff has its own dangling chain stub instead of one short hobble chain joining the ankles. (3) The pull runs across the frame rather than toward the camera. (4) The pen chain runs to the collars by short drop-chains rather than threading through the collars' side rings, which slightly weakens the run-back in 5.5. v04 is rejected. Its ring is intact on an undamaged bracket, so the 'last bolt' beat is lost. The ring's chain also hangs straight down and slack, which contradicts the haul, and no pen plank is shown.

v06 is clean. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, ochre tunic, bandaged hands, and the tunic flap covers his left forearm. His hinged collar has an empty side ring, his wrist manacles are joined by a short chain and his ankles by a hobble chain. Keshavrao matches his lock: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, no ear stud, unbandaged hands, empty collar, wrist chain and hobble. The freed pen chain whips loose and splashes into the water between them, both men stagger apart and look up, and the setting stays inside the closed, lantern-lit hold. Lighting and water level match the chosen 5.4 (v09). There is no text, noose or gore. The panel has no lettering. Minor points that do not block the pick: both men are more muscular than the 'narrow shoulders' note suggests, and the water is shin-deep rather than the waist-deep of 4.5, but it matches the adjacent 5.4. Rejected v03 as backup: Keshavrao's hands are bandaged, which breaks his 'thin unbandaged hands' lock. Each of Nagoji's manacles also trails its own dangling chain instead of a single short chain joining the wrists, so the irons read as broken.

Pick v09. It is the first candidate that stages the whole beat. Nagoji (left) holds up the ring torn out of the splintered beam, and its freed chain splashes into the water. Keshavrao (right of him) hauls on a chain with one bare, cuffed foot braced. In the right half, a ring bolted into sound timber holds, and three collared prisoners have stopped and turn to stare after the pair. The setting is the closed, flooded hold: dark deck beams, hanging glass ship lanterns, no guards, no sky. That matches 5.4, 5.5 and 6.2. Both principals are on model. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair, ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, empty collar and hobble chain, and his left inner forearm is turned away. Keshavrao has hacked-short hair, a faint moustache, the grey-brown tunic, no stud and an empty collar, and both his wrists are manacled. There is no painted text and there are no painted balloons. The main flaw is minor but visible: Nagoji's raised right wrist has only a bandage and no iron cuff, so no wrist chain joins his two hands. If possible, touch up with an iron cuff over that bandage to match his left wrist. Smaller points: the collar rings sit at the front rather than the side (as in earlier accepted frames). Keshavrao's foot presses at the chain rather than clearly kicking the wood, and his hobble chain is only a dangling end. The water is ankle to shin deep, which matches 5.4 and 5.5 but is shallower than the thigh-deep water in 6.2. Lettering space: both balloons at the left fit on the dark ceiling beams. Keshavrao's 'Others.' can go first, in the gap between the two heads (about x 0.22 to 0.37, y 0 to 0.11), with Nagoji's 'Quickly.' in the top-left corner beside his head or just below 'Others.' above his shoulder. The captions fit over the plain dark water along the bottom (y about 0.86 to 1.0) or on the ceiling at upper right. v07 was not acceptable. Every figure hauls in the same galley-crew pose, no chain drops free, and no one is left staring. It is lit by open-flame brass dish lamps on posts, and it has a painted border. It remains the fallback only if v09 is refused.

Minor only. The musket floats half-submerged at the surface in the near foreground instead of lying on the floor under the water. Keshavrao's moustache is a little fuller than 'faint'. A short loose chain hangs from Nagoji's right manacle into the water. Otherwise clean. Nagoji is on the left looking up at the lit hatch, with thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, empty collar with side ring and his left forearm covered by a tunic flap and bandage. Keshavrao is on the right looking at him. Both stand about thigh-deep. The dark ceiling beams across the top (x 0.45 to 0.92, y 0.0 to 0.2) take balloons 0 and 1, and the open water at the bottom centre (x 0.35 to 0.8, y 0.8 to 0.97) takes balloon 2.

Acceptable with a small setting quibble: behind the water is a wooden plank rim that reads a little like a trough edge, and his dhoti looks dry above the waterline, although 6.2 has him thigh-deep. In a tight insert with the bottom caption over most of the water, this reads well enough. v03 shows the lock best: the frizzen stands open above a dry, empty pan. The bandaged, manacled hands grip soundly and the forearms are covered or out of frame. v01 was rejected: Nagoji crouches dry beside a tub with his feet out of the water, contradicting the flooded hold, and his left forearm is bare and exposed.
decisions.erase_note: v04 is an erase-only edit of v03 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with continuity notes. The camera looks up the ladder from a low angle. Nagoji climbs with both manacled, bandaged hands on the rungs and the musket pinned under his near arm, and the hobble chain is visible between his ankle cuffs. He looks back down with moustache, clean chin and gold stud intact, and the brand arm is wrapped. Keshavrao is seen from behind at the foot of the ladder, collar and manacle on, in the water. Notes: (1) Nagoji's iron collar is not visible. His hunched shoulder and long hair hide his neck, so it reads as hidden rather than removed, but it is a soft continuity gap against 6.2. (2) This ladder is round poles lashed with rope, where the ladders in 6.2 and 6.5 are plain wood. (3) A glass lantern and open-flame lamps burn in the hold, which 6.2 does not show. This is allowed in a Portuguese setting but is a small lighting change. Lettering: the Nagoji balloon goes in the dark ceiling at the upper left (x 0.18 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.15), with its tail to his mouth. The caption goes in the dark ceiling beams at the upper right (x 0.66 to 0.97, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Clean. This is Nagoji's point of view straight up the ladder. The guard is a black silhouette on the top rungs, backlit by lightning and rain in the open hatch. The upturned brim and crest of his morion read clearly. One hand grips the ladder rail and the other points the musket barrel down at the camera. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Minor: a dark twisted rope or post shows behind the lower rungs, and this ladder has no rope lashings, unlike 6.4. The GUARD balloon goes on the dark wood planks at the upper right (x 0.72 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.26), with a short tail to the silhouette's mouth under the helmet brim.

Minor only. The camera is low-angle and medium-wide, so the two men read larger than the script's 'small, from a distance'. This matches the previously picked v12. The small gold ear stud cannot be seen at this scale. The rest of the musket barrel is implied behind Nagoji's near arm. His far forearm is partly bare below the cuff, but no brand is drawn. Everything else passes: clean-shaven chin, curled moustache, iron collar, ochre tunic and cream dhoti, bandaged hands, the wrist chain swinging, and one hobble chain joining the ankle cuffs. The guard wears a morion and a buff jerkin, loses his grip, and his musket spins away to the right. The butt strikes his wrist with no injury shown. The hatch is open to lightning and rain, the narrow ladder is fixed, and the lantern-lit hold matches 6.2, 6.4 and 7.2. There is no painted text, no painted balloons and no blood. The dark ceiling beams at top left (about x 0 to 0.33, y 0 to 0.28) hold the long caption, and the dark beams at top right (about x 0.78 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.3) hold 'Bone cracked.'

v08 is clean enough to accept. It is an edit of v07, which r5 accepted, and it fixes v07's guard. The breeches are now dark brown, matching the guard's costume in 7.1 v13, where v07 had maroon. The thing hanging below his belt now reads as a pouch on a strap rather than a possible second leg and boot. The guard is seen from above and behind with his face hidden under the morion: buff jerkin, cross-belts, cream sleeves, sword, arms flung up, and five fingers on each hand. He drops through the gap between two flat treads toward the flood water at the ladder foot, which sets up 7.3. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, hinged collar with its side ring, torn ochre sleeveless tunic and cream dhoti. Both bandaged fists grip one tread in manacles joined by one short chain, and the hands are sound. His cheek is pressed to the rail, eyes shut and face turned from the fall. The near arm is his left, bandaged to mid-forearm, so no brand shows. The setting matches 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4: a lamp-lit timber hold with barrels and a flooded floor, with lightning and rain only down the open hatch shaft. There is no text, blood, noose or anachronism. The panel is silent, so it needs no lettering space. Minor deviations, carried over from v07: a second metal ring still wraps the heel of the visible foot under the ankle cuff, which is small at print size and could be retouched. The guard is lit rather than the script's 'dark shape'. He tumbles jackknifed at the hips with his boots up behind his head, which still reads as a fall. Nagoji's treads sit on a second rail beside the main ladder rail, which only shows if you study it. v07 is an acceptable backup, but its maroon breeches clash with 7.1, and the dark shape below its belt could read as a stray boot.

Clean and faithful to the r3 correction. The view is high, straight down the flat-tread companion ladder, with a brass lamp at left and lashed bales and barrels. The hold is flooded with no dry planks, and the lowest treads meet the water. The fallen guard floats face-down, half submerged, in a buff leather jerkin, cream shirt, dark breeches and boots. His face is hidden in the water and his morion floats beside him. The collared, manacled prisoners press back against the bales, waist-deep. There is no blood, text or noose, and the prisoners' hands are sound. The plain dark hull planking across the top-left (about x 0 to 0.42, y 0 to 0.12) is clear of every face for 'The ladder was clear.' Minor points only: the rendering is more photographic and less inked than 7.1 and 7.4 (the earlier 7.3 candidates shared this and were not faulted for it); the morion floats upright rather than upside down; and the body lies in open water by the barrels rather than pressed against the hull planks.

Clean. This is the r3-approved v03 composition with the painted balloon removed. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light captivity stubble, a small gold ear stud, long curly hair, the empty hinged collar, a torn ochre tunic and a bandaged hand in an iron manacle, its chain running back to the hidden wrist. The visible arm is his right, so the left forearm stays hidden. He is half out of the timber hatch in driving rain, twisted round to shout down at the backs of the prisoners' heads. The flat-tread ladder matches 7.2 and 7.3, and the glass deck lantern is allowed in a Portuguese setting. There is no text, blood or noose. The rain-streaked sky and rigging above and right of his head (about x 0.57 to 0.88, y 0.02 to 0.24) is low-detail and clear of his face for the balloon. Two notes. (1) A cream frame border with a black keyline is painted round the edges (cream to about x 11 and from x 1524, to y 7 and from y 999, with the keyline just inside). Set visible_rect to about [16, 12, 1520, 993] to crop it out. (2) The blurred background deck figures, a sailor in a wide hat at left-centre and a crewman in a brimmed hat at right, have no readable faces and do not read as a guard confronting him.

v13 is acceptable, with small issues. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch3 bible row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, collar with a side ring, wrist chain, ankle cuffs with a hobble chain, bare feet. His left forearm faces outward and the bandage hides the brand. He is braced at the rail, gripping a line, with a loose rope coil at his feet. The storm beat is clear: rain in sheets, lightning, a snapped mainmast leaning with torn canvas, a carved stern castle, barefoot mixed crew in loose shirts and slops, one sailor with a knife in his teeth, men heaving at pump handles. There are no oilskins, uniforms or coats, and no painted text (the carved stern panels are scrollwork only). There is no blood and no noose. Minor points: (1) Nagoji reads as slightly forward of the mast rather than aft, because the stern castle sits beyond the mast from this viewpoint. (2) The red-headcloth sailor's eyes drift toward the right and could be read as glancing at Nagoji. (3) Two small background sailors wear round brimmed hats, a period-plausible sailor's round hat and a cocked hat, not an anachronism. (4) No hatch is visible. There is clear sky for the two captions at the top left (about x 0.07-0.30, y 0.0-0.18, above the capped sailor's head) and the top right (about x 0.78-1.0, y 0.0-0.20, above the wave). Neither covers a face.

v04 is clean and matches the script. It is a high angle down the hatch: Keshavrao's face is turned up with huge eyes and an open mouth, his manacled hands grip the top of the hatch, and below him his bare ankles are hobbled together on a rung in warm lantern light. Lightning and rain show above. He matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown torn tunic, empty iron collar with its ring, no ear stud. The wrist chain is clearly visible between his cuffs, which matches the 8.3 inset. There is no text or pseudo-text; the marks at the bottom are only wood grain on the cross-brace. Minor point: the chain's right end meets the base of the right thumb rather than exactly at the cuff, but it reads as one chain. One hobbled foot is hidden by the beam. 'Sahib!' can sit in the stormy sky at top left (about x 0.06-0.35, y 0.02-0.14) or on the dark deck boards at top right, clear of his face. Backup v03 has the same face and setting, with both hobbled feet visible, but his hands are spread too wide for a short chain and no wrist chain links the cuffs (one chain trails down, the other cuff has a loose ring). That weakens continuity with the 8.3 inset.

v08 is the pick. Nagoji is small in the mid-foreground, seen from behind, braced at the rail. His iron collar has the ring at the side, and his visible right wrist is manacled, chained and bandaged, with the left forearm hidden. A lightning-lit wave rears above the ship. The two insets along the bottom show Keshavrao's manacled hands clamped on the hatch rim with the chain between them, and a shattered spar in the sea. The crew have their backs to him. The painted boxes sit over sky and wave crest, clear of faces. Minor points: the sails look intact, whereas 8.1 has a snapped mainmast. One foreground sailor wears a tricorn and waistcoat, which fits the period but is not the head cloths of 8.1. The spar inset does not show the ship's side. v07 and v06 are the same art without the bandage on his hand. v01 to v05 draw Nagoji large, not small, and show Keshavrao's face in the inset instead of just his hands. In v01 a painted box also covers Keshavrao's eyes.
decisions.erase_note: v09 is an erase-only edit of v08 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: This is the only candidate, and it is usable. The wave crest breaks over the ship's rail and fills the frame, with no figures, no text and no anachronism. Weak points: the frame is 3:2 rather than a narrow strip, so it needs a horizontal crop through the middle band (rail plus curling water). The rail is a light open balustrade rather than the dark solid bulwark of 8.3. The sky is greyer and lighter than the night storm of 8.1 and 8.3, though it can pass as a lightning flash.

Acceptable, with minor deviations. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short hacked hair, a young face, grey-brown tunic, white dhoti, an empty iron collar with a side ring, manacles, and no ear stud. He is half out of the hatch with his left hand clamped on the rim and his right hand at his side, and the inset of Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hand clawing the rope coil sits in the upper left. There is no painted text, balloon, blood or anachronism. Minor points: (1) His moustache is a little heavier than 'faint', but still thin and nothing like Nagoji's curled one. (2) His hair is spiky and wet, not slicked flat, and the hairline graze is barely visible (only a faint mark at the right temple). (3) The right hand reads more as hanging and bracing than as twitching for a missing sword. (4) The wrist chain runs from his right cuff to the waist and vanishes behind the tunic, so the slack between the wrists is vague. (5) In the inset both cuffs, joined by the chain, can read as sitting on one bandaged forearm. At inset size it passes as the chained pair of wrists, and the clawed hand shows 4 digits (thumb plus 3 fingers), which is plausible for the grip. (6) The deck is rain-slick rather than foam-awash, but the grey-white post-wave light fits 9.2. Lettering space: put the caption in the top band of the inset (about x 0.10-0.30, y 0.01-0.18 of the frame), above the fingers, over the blurred background. Put Keshavrao's balloon in the open rain sky at the upper right (about x 0.56-0.95, y 0.02-0.22), with its tail down-left to his mouth.

Minor issues only. v05 and v06 are the same art; only the size of the painted reserves differs. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, collar with side ring, bandaged manacled wrists, ankle irons with hobble chain, torn ochre tunic. His arms are extended at the end of the throw rather than mid-heave, so it reads a little like holding the rope. The rope lies short, halfway across, with coils on the wet deck and water pouring off at the scuppers on the right. Keshavrao (collar, manacles, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, cream dhoti) is already fully out on the deck in front of a raised hatch coaming. In 9.3 he is back half inside the hatch. Each wrist chain dangles from its own cuff rather than visibly linking the pair, and Nagoji's long ochre tunic hem covers most of the cream dhoti. Hands are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism. Lettering: the caption goes in the upper left over the storm sky. Nagoji's balloon fits best in the sky and rigging at top centre, between his head and the mast, with its tail to his mouth. The painted box at the lower right will be covered.
decisions.erase_note: v07 is an erase-only edit of v06 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Keshavrao is half out of the hatch with the rope looped in his manacled hands, and the short wrist chain is caught across the rope. He has the collar with its side ring, faint moustache, short hair and grey-brown tunic, and his hands are sound. The rope runs back across the deck to Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands at the left edge, and the next wave rears on the right with its white edge curling toward the hatch. Nagoji is cut off at the nose by the top edge, so the ear stud is out of frame. Moustache, light stubble and a clean chin show. His ochre cloth drapes over his forearms like sleeves (this keeps the left forearm covered), and Keshavrao's tunic droops over his left upper arm. There is no text and no noose: the loop is at his chest, not his neck. Rejected: v01 (3:2) and v03 have no collar on Keshavrao. v02 has no collar and paints a panel border inside the image, with dark cloud bands above and below.

Minor issues only. This is a medium shot rather than a true wide. The plunging bow is implied by the grey and white wave filling the background rather than drawn. His shin and raised knee rest over and among the coil rather than pressing squarely on it. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear stud, empty collar with side ring, bandaged manacled hands with the chain sagging between the wrists, and a cream dhoti. The ochre drape covers the far (left) forearm. The rope runs dead straight and taut to the right, into the white water. The two caption reserves sit top-left and top-right, clear of his face and hands. Backup v02 is a truer wide: a sleeveless tunic per the sheet, his dhoti knee on the coil, the ankle cuff with hobble chain, and a better 3:1 aspect. But his left forearm is bare from elbow to cuff (outer side toward camera), so it is weaker on the brand-concealment rule. Rejected: v06 has no collar and the rope wraps a bitt. v07 runs a chain from the collar ring to the manacles, so the collar is not empty. v04 and v05 show hands only, with no knee or coil. v03 has no coil. v01 has a 2:1 frame and is weaker.
decisions.erase_note: v09 is an erase-only edit of v08 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The bandages are stripped into long trailing strips but not visibly scorched, and the palms are only mildly reddened. There is no torn flesh and no blood. Both open palms face the viewer with thumbs to the viewer's right, so the handedness is slightly ambiguous, but it reads naturally at print size. The knee pinning the coil is under the ochre tunic hem here, while in 9.4 v08 the cream dhoti shows at the knee. The staging matches the script. The rope has parted at a frayed end on the coil side of his hands, the free length slides through his open palms toward the rail and the spray at the right, his knee pins the coil, and the manacles are linked by their short chain. The two caption reserves sit top-left over the tunic and top-right over the rain and rigging, clear of the hands. Rejected: v01 to v07 all break the rope between his two hands. v04 to v06 also lack the knee and coil, v07's wrist cuffs are not linked, and v01 and v02 are 3:2.
decisions.erase_note: v09 is an erase-only edit of v08 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Minor: the ladder in the hatch reads as intact, not clearly broken, and Nagoji is a medium-size figure rather than 'small' in the frame. Everything else matches: empty hatch with water pouring into the hold, nobody there, empty hinged collar with its ring, wrist chain, hobble chain, reddened open palms trailing bandage strips, and the frayed rope coil at his feet. Face matches the sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud). His left forearm is covered by the tunic sleeve. The top-right painted box sits over sky and rigging. The other candidates fail. v03 is the same art but with the left inner forearm bare and turned to camera, which breaks the hidden-brand rule. v01 and v02 also show the bare left forearm, and they put a loose bandage strip at his feet where the frayed rope coil should be.
decisions.erase_note: v05 is an erase-only edit of v04 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: Minor only: the comrade's horse is drawn lying fallen beside him rather than standing riderless, which still reads as the script's beat. The cast list includes Keshavrao, but the beat comes after he is lost, so his absence is correct. I picked v08 over the otherwise identical v09 because its riders wear rust turbans with a red sash, which matches the Maratha cavalry dress in the bible. v09's white turbans could read as the Madurai troop. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, stubbled clean-shaven chin, gold stud, collar with side ring and torn ochre tunic. There is no painted text, and the riders are faceless backs. The sky at top left and the dust at bottom left give clear caption space over the memory stain, away from his face.
decisions.override: orchestrator: CONTINUITY.md standing rule, background Maratha riders in memory panels wear white or cream angarkhas and pagdis, never Nagoji's rust-red turban and sash; confirmed by the five-lens reviews r3 (continuity and rules). The selector's reading of the bible was wrong.

decisions.issues: v03: profile at the rail, facing out to sea. Two turns of rope round his chest pulled tight by bandaged, manacled hands, frayed free end trailing, empty collar with ring, joined wrist chain, and a ragged tunic flap and bandage over the far (left) forearm. The splintered, barnacled spar rides the foam. The hobble chain is out of frame because of the waist-up crop, and the spar sits mid-distance rather than directly below. There is open storm sky right of his face for the 'Forgive me' balloon. Rejected: v01 (Portuguese guards on deck, not in the beat), v04 (rope tied to the spar and a hauling pose), v05 (hands on the rail, no knotting), v06 (hands behind his back and no collar), v07 (confused staging with no rail between him and the sea).
decisions.erase_note: v08 is an erase-only edit of v03 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: v07 is the only candidate whose wrists stay joined by the short wrist chain. It also shows the hobble chain at the ankles, the collar, two turns of rope round his chest with the frayed end trailing, both forearms under tunic flap and bandage, lightning sky, black water, and the ship's rail behind him. Face matches (moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Caveat: he leaps screen-left with the ship on the right, the reverse of 10.3 where he faces screen-right toward the sea. That break in screen direction is acceptable across the cut, but a horizontal flip would restore continuity if the page reads awkwardly (both forearms are covered, so a flip is safe for the brand rule). Rejected: v02 (arms flung wide, only one wrist chained, rope rising from behind his neck), v03, v04 and v05 (arms spread with separate chain stubs on each wrist, implying a broken wrist chain), v01 (guards reaching from the rail, arms spread), v06 (a wrist chain and ankle chain running back to the ship, a gold hoop at the neck).
decisions.erase_note: v08 is an erase-only edit of v07 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited

decisions.issues: v04: underwater just below the white foam of his entry, looking up past him. Collar with ring, gold stud, moustache and clean chin match. Joined manacles and fists at the bottom edge, rope knotted round his chest, and the rope's free end snakes up toward the barnacled, splintered spar without being tied to it. The ship's dark hull heels away beyond. Minor: at extreme zoom a few barnacles have hole patterns that faintly suggest faces, but at print size they read as barnacles. Rejected: v01 and v02 (rope lashed around the spar instead of a free end), v03 (collar drawn split in two floating pieces, rope ends on the spar, 3:2 format), v05 (no collar, reddish marks on the shoulders, spar reads as part of the hull).
decisions.erase_note: v06 is an erase-only edit of v04 (painted balloons removed); tails, faces and keep zones inherited
